items.stem: A neutropenic patient on chemotherapy develops a fever of 38.5C. How should the nurse interpret this?

options.text: A minor issue to recheck next day
options.rationale: Fever in neutropenia is urgent, not routine.

options.text: A potential oncologic emergency (febrile neutropenia) needing prompt action
options.rationale: Correct: fever with neutropenia is a medical emergency requiring prompt evaluation and treatment.
Febrile neutropenia always warrants prompt action.

options.text: A sign the cancer is cured
options.rationale: Fever is unrelated to cure and signals possible infection.

items.explanation: Correct: fever with neutropenia is a medical emergency requiring prompt evaluation and treatment.

items.stem: What is the best characterisation of palliative care?

options.text: Care provided only in the final days of life
options.rationale: That describes a narrow end-of-life phase, not palliative care overall.

options.text: Symptom- and quality-of-life-focused care that can accompany active treatment
options.rationale: Correct: palliative care focuses on symptoms and quality of life and may run alongside curative treatment.

options.text: Care that stops all symptom management
options.rationale: Palliative care centres on symptom management.
Palliative care is a care approach, not a chemotherapy regimen.

items.explanation: Correct: palliative care focuses on symptoms and quality of life and may run alongside curative treatment.

items.stem: Which TWO are recognised oncologic emergencies the nurse must act on quickly?

options.text: Spinal cord compression with new neurologic deficits
options.rationale: Correct: spinal cord compression is a true oncologic emergency.

options.text: Tumor lysis syndrome with metabolic derangement
options.rationale: Correct: tumor lysis syndrome is a recognised oncologic emergency.

options.text: Mild transient fatigue after a clinic visit
options.rationale: Mild fatigue is common and not an emergency.
A healed scar is not an emergency.

items.explanation: Correct: spinal cord compression is a true oncologic emergency.
